segments.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָיוּ כּוֹרְתִין עֵצִים לַעֲשׂוֹת פֶּחָמִין לַעֲשׂוֹת בַּרְזֶל בְּשַׁבָּת, בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הָיוּ אוֹכְלִין בְּשַׂר עוֹף בְּחָלָב.
segments.en: We learned in our mishna: «And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said:» One may even cut down trees to prepare charcoal for the purpose of circumcision on Shabbat. With regard to this issue, «the Sages taught» in a baraita: «In the locale of Rabbi Eliezer,» where they would follow his ruling, «they would» even «cut down trees» on Shabbat «to prepare charcoal» from it in order «to fashion iron» tools with which to circumcise a child «on Shabbat.» On a related note, the baraita relates: «In the locale of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili they would eat poultry meat in milk,» as Rabbi Yosei HaGelili held that the prohibition of meat in milk does not include poultry.
